tb_estimate_alpha — 2D typed op

• Data kinds: points → feature

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "tb_estimate_alpha", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

Stages (the ops that come before → this op, left to right):

▸ tb_estimate_alpha: stages (docs site)

Usage

Returns a recommended alpha based on the scale of the point cloud (based on the median nearest-neighbor distance).

Finds the median m of each point's nearest-neighbour distance and returns alpha = 1/(2m) so that the radius threshold is 1/alpha ≈ 2m (allowing up to about 2 times the neighbour spacing). This keeps the well-behaved tetrahedra near the surface while cutting off greatly stretched tetrahedra (= concavities, outside). Duplicate points have nearest-neighbour distance 0, so only positive distances are used.

Parameters

points : array_like (N,3)

Returns

alpha : float

A positive finite value.

The 3d op estimate_alpha bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). This op has no tuning points; neither a nor b is used.
